newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit recoups against dollar.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit recoups against dollar.

text.p: A stronger U.S. dollar in Asia kept most currencies in thin defensive trade on Tuesday, but with some rises capped by intervention fears.
Malaysia's ringgit drifted past significant support at 2.51 against the dollar early, spurred by investment bank demand.
Dealers said the dollar's rise was capped later by selling of dollar/ringgit on intervention by Bank Negara.
"Investment banks were buying sizeable amounts until Bank Negara started checking," a Japanese bank dealer said.
Another dealer with a local bank confirmed the central bank's checking, which restrained the dollar's rise.
Dollar/ringgit was at 2.5090/2.5095 at 0430 GMT against 2.5070/2.5080 late on Monday.
The Indonesian rupiah was also slightly weaker against the dollar due to sufficient liquidity.

Corporates due for weekly tax settlements on Tuesday and the hike in statutory reserve requirements appeared able to meet demand, which was helped by central bank injection of 847 billion rupiah on Tuesday, dealers said.
The new reserve rate of five percent, which takes effect on Wednesday, was expected to drain five to eight trillion rupiah.
Liquidity, however, should keep rupiah well supported at 2,409 against its U.S. counterpart, although dollar strength overseas may inhibit the rate's upside, analysts said.
Dollar/rupiah was at 2,405.60/2,406.00 compared with 2,404.50/2,404.75 in late Monday action.
In Singapore, dollar/Sing activity was subdued with the local currency continuing its longer-term descent against the greenback on anticipation of higher U.S. interest rates.
"Some ringgit/Sing buying in the morning also worked against the Sing," the dealer with the European broking house said.
Dollar/Sing eased to 1.4415/1.4425 at mid-session, down from 1.4380/90 on Monday.
Dealers said the Singapore currency looked set to fluctuate within a 1.4300 to 1.4500 band, tending toward its recent low of 1.4520 on the dollar's bullish fundamentals.
Little interest was sighted for the Thai baht, dampened by the four-day Thai New Year holiday which began on Saturday.
Dealers said outrights had eased marginally to 26.090/26.095 compared with 26.070/26.075 on Monday, and forwards were also holding a bearish tone with buyers sidelined.
The Bank of Thailand last fixed the daily baht/dollar mid-rate at 26.07 on Friday.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), James Mclean in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Jacqueline Wong in Singapore (65-8703088)
